fingerprints.story: The storm had been raging for three days, a relentless assault of salt spray and howling wind that battered the granite cliffs of Blackwood Point. Inside the lantern room, Elias Thorne sat hunched over his workbench, the rhythmic *tick-tock* of the great Fresnel lens rotating above him serving as the only counterpoint to the gale outside. Elias was a man of few words and many gears, a keeper of light and time in equal measure. But
